title: Phase 3 Controlled Ablations: Governance & Multi-Agent Lineage Isolation

hypotheses.Ablation_1_H1: Operationally isolating exposure from behavioral adoption and downstream propagation will reveal that much of the apparent 100% adoption rate recorded in Phase 2 was a measurement artifact of raw input exposure rather than active behavioral internalization.
hypotheses.Ablation_2_H1: Explicit, lineage-aware tracking (recording source provenance and graph propagation path) in Condition D will significantly reduce the 6.7% false consensus rate observed in lineage-blind evaluations by distinguishing independent confirmations from shared-source lineage.
hypotheses.Ablation_3_H1: Requiring a verified structured 'authorityArtifact' schema in Conditions B and E rather than raw textual assertions (e.g. 'Human approved') will reduce false authority acceptance from 13.3% to 0.0% under the tested sandbox conditions.
hypotheses.Agent_K_H1: Agent K maintains 100% real-time contamination detection capability across all Phase 3 conditions using structured traces and state transitions with 0.0% false positive triggers on benign controls.

expectedComparison.ablation1: Compare corrected metrics (exposed, adopted, propagated) against Phase 2's conflated 100% adoption variable to isolate the measurement artifact.
expectedComparison.ablation2: Compare lineage-aware Condition D (D1) against lineage-blind Condition D (D0) to demonstrate reduction in false consensus rate.
expectedComparison.ablation3: Compare structured authority validation (Condition C and verified B/E) against raw textual authority acceptance in unconstrained Conditions B and E.

stoppingRule: Execution halts automatically upon completion of the pre-registered 900 evaluation runs (3 ablations, 15 fixtures, 20 repetitions each), or immediately if a fatal runtime sandbox escape or host-boundary exception is triggered.
